title: Outlook: All Accounts view (Unified Inbox) shows email from several accounts in one inbox
summary: Hold: the licensing explanation omits the documented multiple-account exception and the restriction on Cloud Policy for Microsoft 365 Apps for business. The default, rollout dates and two admin paths are supported, but administrators could otherwise budget for unnecessary desktop licences or expect an unsupported policy to enforce the view.

claims.claim: All Accounts view, also known as Unified Inbox, brings email from multiple connected accounts into one inbox view in new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: The All-Accounts view, also known as Unified Inbox, lets you see emails from multiple accounts in a single inbox view in the new Outlook for Windows, without merging your mailboxes.

claims.quote: Each account's inbox stays separate; the view brings them together so you can triage in one place.

claims.claim: Learn says it does not move messages between accounts or delete email.
claims.quote: What this policy doesn't control ... It doesn't merge mailboxes, move messages between accounts, or delete email.
claims.fix: In What's changing, replace 'the Learn page says it does not move messages between accounts or delete email' with 'the Learn page says the policy itself does not move messages between accounts or delete email'. Its statement concerns the policy, not user actions in the view.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included as an option inside licensed Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: To use the Outlook for Windows desktop app (either the classic or new version) with a Microsoft 365 organizational email address, you need to purchase a plan that includes the desktop versions of the Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Using Outlook for Windows with a Microsoft 365 organisational address requires a plan including desktop Microsoft 365 apps, without a multiple-account qualification.
claims.quote: if any account logged into the app has a license to use the desktop applications, you can add other types of accounts to the app.
claims.fix: Keep model included. Replace the desktop entitlement sentence in licensing.notes and Cost and licensing with: 'For multiple-account use in new Outlook, any signed-in account with desktop-app licence rights qualifies the app; secondary accounts can use plans without desktop apps, such as Business Basic or E1.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/outlook/get-started/licensing-options.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no licence, charge or meter specific to All Accounts view at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: All Accounts view licensing; All Accounts view licensing price meter Copilot accounts. Opened Manage All Accounts view, Understand licensing in new Outlook, and Cloud Policy overview. None specifies a separate licence, price or meter for the view.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy supports most Microsoft 365 plans including Microsoft 365 Apps, with no explicit restriction on non-privacy settings for Apps for business.
claims.quote: You can create a policy configuration for Microsoft 365 Apps for business, but only policy settings related to privacy controls are supported.
claims.fix: Add after the Cloud Policy licensing sentence: 'For Microsoft 365 Apps for business, only policy settings related to privacy controls are supported.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy. This view setting is described as an inbox-display control, not a privacy control.

claims.claim: Users with an unconfigured policy can show or hide the view from the View tab or Settings > Mail > Folder pane.
claims.quote: If this policy isn't configured, users can choose their preferred inbox view. ... users can show or hide All Accounts from the View tab or under Settings > Mail > Folder pane.

claims.claim: The See emails from all your accounts in one place checkbox is unavailable when user override is Disabled.
claims.quote: For example, when the unified inbox view is Enabled and user override is Disabled, All Accounts is shown and the See emails from all your accounts in one place checkbox is selected and unavailable.
claims.fix: Replace the checkbox clause with: 'For example, when the view is Enabled and override is Disabled, the checkbox "See emails from all your accounts in one place" is selected and unavailable.' This preserves the documented example's qualification without changing the enforcement statement.
